definition.hypothesis: If the WorkloadContract, the selected EnvironmentBinding, the versioned platform defaults, and the renderer revision are fixed, the render path produces the same complete claim-relevant release input for the V1 synchronous workload on every render. A claim-relevant contract change changes only the output it owns. Invalid and conflicting inputs are refused with a stable category and code. The release input deploys and serves a real completion, and no claim-relevant workload intent is written again by hand after rendering.
definition.scope: E01 tests the front of the V2 path: contract, render, and release input, and in E01-D also Git, Argo CD, and one served completion. E01 injects no fault and tests no failure tolerance.

outcomeStates.PASSED: Every acceptance criterion of the part held.
outcomeStates.FAILED: The part executed as registered, and at least one acceptance criterion did not hold. A FAILED run is valid evidence and stays recorded.
outcomeStates.INCONCLUSIVE: The part executed and could not answer its question: a check it needs did not run, or its evidence is incomplete.
outcomeStates.REFUSED: The part did not start, because a precondition failed.
outcomeStates.ABORTED: The part started and met an abort condition. The run records the condition and the cleanup.

preconditions: This record, or a later revision of it, is merged. The run records the merged commit it executes, as a full Git revision.
The working tree at that commit is clean.

The content digest of every pinned input at that commit equals its pin, or a merged later revision of this record classifies the change. python -m tools.experiment_freeze --changes lists the inputs that differ.
E01-D only: a merged revision of this record names the environment identity. While the environment identity is pending, E01-D is REFUSED.
definition.repetitionRule: No run is repeated to obtain a different outcome. After an INCONCLUSIVE, REFUSED, or ABORTED run, a new run may follow. Every run stays recorded with its outcome state.
definition.notResultEvidence: Checks that ran before this record merged are not E01 runs and are not result evidence. These are the repository's test suites, which already exercise double renders, a replica-count mutation, and refusals, and a one-time check during registration that each expected refusal below is the one the published rule table assigns. An E01 part counts only when it runs, after this record merges, as registered here.
limitations: The platform-defaults revision a release records is asserted. Nothing reconstructs the defaults from it, so the release does not prove which defaults it was rendered from.

Two hand-written strings repeat contract pins: the model's download URL and its licence reference. E01-AC5 and E01-AC10 do not cover them. The acquisition job's check against the generated model.artifact.sha256 is what refuses other bytes.
Nothing blocks a merge that changes a pinned input. The precondition refuses the run until a merged revision classifies the change.
E01-C-4 is refused by the binding parser, which publishes a code and a field and no rule category.
E01-A, E01-B, and E01-C use one contract on one binding.
doesNotEstablish: That E01-D can run before its environment identity is frozen.

parts.title: Deterministic double render
parts.question: Do two renders of identical inputs produce identical release input that records its sources?

inputs.platformDefaults: Version v1alpha1: the requestTimeoutMs, drainTimeoutMs, and maxOutputTokens values of the api block of charts/inferops-llm/values.yaml, read as tools/generated_release reads them.
inputs.renderer: HelmValuesRenderer from src/inferops/domain/render, constructed with the executing commit as its revision.

procedure: Load the compatibility matrix. Parse the contract with parse_workload_contract and the binding with parse_environment_binding.

Call generate_release with the renderer, the contract, the platform defaults, the binding, and binding_name local-kind. generate_release validates the contract and builds the render context before it renders.
Write the result with write_release to render-a, a directory that does not exist before the call.
In a second Python process, with a different PYTHONHASHSEED, repeat the three steps above and write to render-b.
Compare render-a with render-b: the bytes of values.generated.yaml, the bytes of rendered-workload-release.yaml, the SHA-256 of each file, and metadata.releaseId.

Check the provenance of render-a against values computed apart from the release: source.contract.sha256 against contract_digest of the parsed contract; the source.environmentBinding name, apiVersion, and sha256 against local-kind, inferops.io/v1alpha1, and binding_digest of the parsed binding; output.helmValues.sha256 against the SHA-256 of the bytes of render-a/values.generated.yaml; source.renderer.revision and source.platformDefaults.revision against the executing commit.
Admit the hand-written values beside the render-a values with admit_manual_values.
List every chart value that a workload-intent context value renders to, from HELM_VALUE_DISPOSITIONS and RENDER_FIELD_OWNERSHIP, and check that each is in render-a/values.generated.yaml.

Merge the chart's defaults, render-a/values.generated.yaml, and the hand-written values the way Helm merges values files. Merge the chart's defaults and the V1 real values the same way. List every value that differs.

parts.title: Intent mutation
parts.question: Does one claim-relevant contract change move only the output it owns?
parts.rationale: The runtime replica count is claim-relevant workload intent with a known deployment effect. The chart runs a fixed replica count, so the range is set to one number, inside the chart's limit of 16.
procedure: Apply the mutation, as JSON Patch operations, to the contract document as read from YAML, before parse_workload_contract.
Render and write as in E01-A steps 1 to 3, to mutation, a directory that does not exist before the call.
Compare mutation with render-a of the same run: list every leaf of values.generated.yaml that differs, with both values, and every field of rendered-workload-release.yaml that differs.
Check that source.contract.sha256 in mutation equals contract_digest of the mutated contract.

parts.title: Negative contract and refusal cases
parts.question: Are invalid and conflicting inputs refused deterministically, with the expected stable category and code?

inputs.cases: The cases below. An edit is a JSON Patch operation, applied to the document as read from YAML before it is parsed. An input a case does not list is the E01-A input.

procedure: For each case, build its inputs from the pinned files and the edits it lists.

Run the step the case names. For generate_release and parse_environment_binding, parse the inputs and call generate_release as in E01-A. For admit_manual_values, call it with the values of the E01-A render and the edited hand-written values.
Record the refusal: its exception type, and for each finding in order, its rule identifier, category, code, and field. For a refusal with no findings, record its code and field.
Check that the case's output directory does not exist after the case.
Run each case a second time in the same way, and compare the two refusals.

cases.description: The contract's synchronousLlm block is absent. The schema requires it for the synchronous-llm profile.
The contract's minimum replica count exceeds its maximum. Each value is valid alone; together they are not.
The hand-written values set runtime.replicaCount, which the contract owns and the renderer generates.

inputs.generatedValues: The values of the E01-A render

cases.description: The binding supplies spec.scaling, the replica range the contract owns. The binding's schema has no field for it, so the binding parser refuses the document before the render boundary sees it.

expected.categoryNote: The binding parser publishes a code and a field. It publishes no rule category, so none is expected.

cases.description: A valid mock-llm contract, with a binding that serves its ci environment. The renderer takes the synchronous-llm profile only.
The contract asks for the balanced runtime profile. The chart configures one runtime sizing, resource-conscious.

parts.title: Real deployment
parts.question: Does the release rendered from the unmodified contract deploy through Git and Argo CD and serve a real completion?

inputs.environmentBinding: The binding the environment identity names.
inputs.handWrittenValues: One hand-written values file for the environment, which the environment identity names. It is admitted beside the generated values with no finding.

procedure: Render the release from the inputs above and write it with write_release.
Commit the generated release to the Git desired state, at the binding's spec.gitops.destinationPath.
Let Argo CD reconcile the desired state into the cluster. The release takes its values from the generated values file and the admitted hand-written values file only, with no parameter override.

Wait until the API's readiness endpoint answers 200 and the runtime pod is Ready. The wait is bounded by the startup budget the chart renders for the runtime, counted from the moment Argo CD reports the desired revision synced.
Send one request to the API Service: POST /v1/chat/completions, with model set to the generated model.identifier, one user message, and stream false.
Verify the identities named in E01-AC9 against the release, Argo CD, and the running pods.

value.definition: This record states the hypothesis, the parts, the procedure, and the acceptance criteria in full. A change to any of them is a new revision of this record.

value.pinnedInputs: Every file on the experiment path is pinned by its content digest in pinnedInputs. A record cannot name the commit that merges it, so the pins freeze the path, not a commit.
value.executingRevision: Each run records the merged commit it executes, as a full Git revision, and checks the pinned inputs at that commit before it starts.

value.kind: static: the parts render, write files, and refuse in memory
value.model: none: no model artifact is read or loaded
value.toolchain: Python 3.12 with the dependencies uv.lock pins, run with uv run --locked
value.recordedPerRun: The host's operating system and version, the Python version, and the uv version

environmentIdentity.reason: E01-D needs a real cluster with Argo CD reconciling from Git, and that environment does not exist yet. The freeze revision that names it is owned by V2-S3-004-PR1. E01-D is REFUSED while this entry is pending.

callerProfileRevision.reason: No caller sends a request: the parts render and refuse in memory.
E01-D sends one completion to show the path serves, and its procedure fixes the request. It runs no caller workload profile, and it makes no claim about caller outcomes under load.

value.runtimeReplicas: 1, from spec.scaling of the unmodified reference contract
value.apiReplicas: The spec.platform.apiReplicas of the binding the environment identity names: 1 in both committed local bindings
value.delivery: Argo CD reconciles the release from the Git desired state at that binding's spec.gitops.destinationPath

fault.reason: E01 injects no fault. It tests whether workload intent becomes release input and a served completion, not tolerance of a failure.

repetitionCount.value: One run of two renders, under definition.repetitionRule.
One mutated render in the same run as E01-A, compared with that run's render-a, under definition.repetitionRule.
One run in which each of the six cases executes twice, under definition.repetitionRule.
One real deployment with one completion, under definition.repetitionRule.

value.statement: The two renders are canonically identical: both files are byte-identical, the SHA-256 of each file is equal, and metadata.releaseId is equal.
The release records the source contract digest, and it equals contract_digest of the parsed contract.
The release records the EnvironmentBinding's name, apiVersion, and digest, and they equal local-kind, inferops.io/v1alpha1, and binding_digest of the parsed binding.

The release records the generated values digest, and it equals the SHA-256 of the bytes of the values file beside it. The renderer and platform-defaults revisions it records equal the executing commit.

No claim-relevant workload intent is written by hand after rendering: admit_manual_values admits the hand-written values with no finding; every chart value that a workload-intent context value renders to is in the generated values file; and the generated and hand-written values, merged over the chart's defaults, equal the V1 real values merged the same way, except telemetry.deploymentEnvironment, which is local in V2 and dev in V1 as the V1 synchronous compatibility record states.

The mutation changes only the expected semantic output: in values.generated.yaml, only runtime.replicaCount, from 1 to 2; in rendered-workload-release.yaml, only metadata.releaseId, output.helmValues.sha256, and source.contract.sha256; and source.contract.sha256 equals contract_digest of the mutated contract.

Every negative case is refused at its registered step with its expected refusal: for a RenderRefused, exactly the registered findings, in order, each with its rule, category, code, and field; for E01-C-4, the registered exception type, code, and field. No case writes an output directory, and each case's second execution gives the same refusal as its first.

The release rendered from the unmodified reference contract, accepted into Git and reconciled by Argo CD, produces at least one real successful completion: HTTP 200, with at least one choice whose assistant message is not empty.

The deployed identities verify against the release: the desired-state revision Argo CD reports as synced holds the generated release; the release records the contract, binding, and values digests, and they match their sources and the values file; the running runtime container's image digest is the generated runtime.image.digest; the model revision the runtime reads is the generated model.revision; and the API serves the model under the generated model.identifier.

No claim-relevant workload intent is written by hand after rendering: the release is installed from the generated values file and one hand-written values file only, with no parameter override, and admit_manual_values admits that hand-written file beside the generated values with no finding.

derivedNumericBounds.reason: No E01 criterion is a timing or caller-outcome bound, and the runtime-startup and stable-caller qualifications have not run. The E01-D readiness wait is bounded by the startup budget the chart renders. That is an operational limit, not a derived acceptance bound.

files.render-a/ and render-b/: The two E01-A renders, as write_release wrote them.
files.refusals.json: The two recorded refusals of each E01-C case.
files.result.md: Each criterion, its verdict, and the evidence it rests on, with the limitations first.

files.run.v1alpha1.json: The run manifest, as for E01-A, with the environment identity.
files.release/: The two generated files as committed to the Git desired state.
files.argo.json: The Argo CD application status at verification, with credentials removed.
files.pods.json: The API and runtime pods, with their image digests.
files.completion.json: The request, and the response's status, model, and text length. The generated text is not kept.
files.result.md: Each criterion, its verdict, and the evidence it rests on, with the limitations first.

Runtime: a real cluster, Argo CD, the real runtime, and the real model serve one completion. One environment and one run; not representative.
